about.title: Desert Hot Springs Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Desert Hot Springs sits in Riverside County, where construction, hospitality, and agriculture jobs are common, and so are on-the-job injuries. Workers hurt on the clock often assume workers' compensation is their only option, but that's not always true. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on roads like Palm Drive or Hacienda Avenue contributed to the accident, a separate third-party injury claim may be possible alongside a workers' comp filing. Navigating both systems at once can be confusing, especially while recovering from an injury and dealing with missed paychecks. Our team can help you sort out which claims apply and what deadlines matter. Attorneys on our team work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

items.title: We Help Sort Out Which Claim Applies
items.desc: California workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party can open the door to a separate injury claim. We can help you figure out if that applies to your situation.

items.title: Deadlines Matter and We Help You Move Fast
items.desc: Employer injury reports are generally due within 30 days, while third-party injury claims carry a two-year deadline in California. Missing either window can limit your options, so timing matters.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, and You Deserve Support
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury or file a claim. Reaching out to us early can help protect your rights if you're worried about pushback at work.

items.question: I was hurt working near Dillon Road — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, you'll still file a workers' compensation claim with your employer since that's usually the exclusive remedy regardless of fault. But if a third party, like a subcontractor, driver, or equipment maker, contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate injury claim worth exploring. We can help you understand which paths apply to your specific situation.

items.question: What if my employer in Desert Hot Springs tries to punish me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: California law makes it illegal for employers to retaliate against workers who report an on-the-job injury or file a workers' comp claim. If you're facing pushback, documenting what happens and speaking with us can help protect your rights moving forward.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free consultation. Attorneys work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
